newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada bonds close with rally amid U.S. gains.
newsitem.headline: Canada bonds close with rally amid U.S. gains.

text.p: Canadian bonds closed higher boosted by U.S. strength on Tuesday as both markets rebounded from Monday's decline, analysts said.

"We're up in Canada on the back of the U.S.," said Toronto-Dominion Securities economist Richard Wylie. Today's weaker-than-forecast U.S. economic data allowed bonds to recover. The National Association of Purchasing Management's activity index fell to 51.7 in September from 52.6 last month.
Canada's 30-year benchmark bond rose C$0.67 at C$104.07 to yield 7.639 percent against the U.S. 30-year benchmark which gained 19/32 to yield 6.88 percent.
The spread between the benchmark bonds was 76 basis points, unchanged from Monday's close.

"The market had been bracing for some pretty bad news," Wylie said. Economists had forecast a reading of 52.5. Canada's market gained for a second day, while the U.S. market recovered from its decline on Monday.
Investors are awaiting the more important U.S. employment data on Friday, which include nonfarm payrolls numbers and the unemployment rate, both for September.
Today the Bank of Canada set a round of special purchase and resale agreements at 4.25 percent.
The overnight lending rate had traded above the 3.75-4.25 percent range set by Canada's central bank.
In other prices, the 7.0 percent of 2006 rose C$0.46 to C$99.03 to yield 7.069 percent. The U.S. 10-year benchmark rose 14/32 to yield 6.64 percent.
The spread between the two benchmark bonds was 43 basis points, unchanged from Monday's close.
The three-month cash bill traded at 3.64 percent against the U.S. three-month bill at 5.10 percent.
